html:
The Battles of the Isonzo were twelve battles fought from 1915 to 1917 along the Soča River, called the Isonzo in Italian, in today's western Slovenia, between Italy and Austria Hungary.

Italy joined World War I in 1915 hoping to take Austrian lands at the head of the Adriatic. Its armies attacked again and again up mountain slopes, gaining little ground at huge cost. Many of the defenders were Slovenes fighting for their homes. In the twelfth battle, in October 1917, German and Austrian troops broke through at Kobarid, the Caporetto of Italian accounts, and drove the Italians back to the Piave. Ernest Hemingway's A Farewell to Arms is set there. After the war Italy gained the area anyway.
